proposal.hypothesis: Using a zero-based x index from line pointers already positioned at x0 avoids applying the interior offset twice and presents a contiguous loop to the compiler. Prior valid OpenMP SIMD candidates show this directive is supported in the measured build; checking the actual input, velocity, and output line starts enables an aligned SIMD path only when all three satisfy the 16-byte condition, with an unaligned SIMD fallback. The guarded, unpeeled formulation is distinct from prior scalar peeling variants, and its performance remains to be measured.

retained: Keep the timestep kernel unfused and preserve its existing z/y interior bounds, arithmetic order, parity, buffers, and interface.
Form each line pointer at row_base + x0, then traverse the line with x from zero to x1 - x0 so the interior offset is applied once.
At runtime, test the actual input, velocity, and output line-pointer addresses; use aligned OpenMP SIMD only if all are 16-byte aligned, otherwise use unaligned OpenMP SIMD.
Guard explicit SIMD for OpenMP 4.0 or later and retain a scalar loop when that support is unavailable; do not add threading, blocking, compiler flags, or ISA-specific code.
